COCO analysis (Li et al. 2018)

Source: R/coco_classic.R
coco_classic.Rd

Correlation coefficient between the (AR(1)-corrected) data periodogram and an astronomical target over a grid of sedimentation rates, with the H0 (no orbital forcing) Monte Carlo test of Li et al. (2018). Translated from Acycle corrcoefslices.m / cyclecorr.m (Mingsong Li).

Usage

coco_classic(
  data,
  target,
  orbit = NULL,
  sr = seq(0.2, 20, by = 0.2),
  dt = NULL,
  pad = 5000,
  red = 1,
  nsim = 0,
  slices = 1,
  adjust = 0,
  method = c("Pearson", "Spearman"),
  seed = NULL,
  keep_null = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Record to analyse (matrix or data frame; the first two columns are used): depth in metres in column 1 and the proxy in column 2, evenly spaced (it is not interpolated; incomplete rows are dropped and the rows sorted by depth). Required, no default.

target

Astronomical target periodogram (two-column matrix or data frame): frequency in cycles/kyr in column 1 and power in column 2, e.g. the output of coco_target_from_periods, coco_target_from_series. Its peaks higher than half the mean power are rebuilt as Gaussian peaks with the Rayleigh width of the data at every tested rate. Required, no default.

orbit

Astronomical periods in kyr (numeric vector), used to count how many astronomical parameters contribute at each rate (and, with adjust=1, to define the target bands; then seven periods are needed). NULL uses the periods stored with the target (attribute "orbit", set by coco_target_from_periods), or else the seven periods of Li et al. (2018) (400, 120.5, 93.1, 38.6, 23.0, 21.8 and 18.5 kyr). Default=NULL.

sr

Sedimentation rates to test, in cm/kyr (numeric vector, > 0). Default=seq(0.2, 20, by = 0.2).

dt

Sampling interval of data, in metres (numeric, > 0); NULL uses the median spacing of the depth column. Default=NULL.

pad

Length (number of points) to which the data (or each slice) is zero-padded for the periodogram (integer, at least the number of samples); a larger value gives a finer frequency grid. Default=5000.

red

Red-noise treatment of the data periodogram (integer): 0 none; 1 the AR(1) background is subtracted (as in Li et al. 2018); 2 the periodogram is divided by the AR(1) background minus 1; 3 a robust AR(1) background (median-smoothed spectrum) is subtracted; a value from 50 to 99 divides by that AR(1) confidence level (in %) minus 1, so only power above it remains. Negative values are set to zero. Default=1.

nsim

Number of Monte Carlo simulations of the null hypothesis of no astronomical forcing (random spectra with as many peaks as the data spectrum), used for the p-value p_h0 and pCOCO (integer, >= 0; 2000 in Li et al. 2018); 0 skips them. Default=0.

slices

Number of equal-depth slices whose periodograms are averaged (integer, >= 1); 1 uses the whole record. Default=1.

adjust

Adjust the power of the target in four bands (long eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity, precession) to the power of the data in those bands at each rate (integer): 0 no, 1 yes (only for a seven-period target). Default=0.

method

Correlation coefficient between the data and target spectra (character): "Pearson" (as in Li et al. 2018) or "Spearman". Default=c("Pearson", "Spearman"), i.e. "Pearson".

seed

Seed of the random number generator (integer), so that the Monte Carlo results can be reproduced; NULL leaves the current random state unchanged. Default=NULL.

keep_null

Return the Monte Carlo null correlations (matrix, rates in rows, simulations in columns) as element null of the output (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

verbose

Print progress messages of the Monte Carlo simulations (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

Value

list with data.frame `result` (sr, rho, p_param, p_h0, norbit, pcoco)
